serviceBoundary.message: Two recent enquiries expected me to manage all their social content. I actually help them choose a direction and make a practical plan; I do not run their channels. How could we make that clearer without inventing a new niche?

response.response: You can make your scope clearer by naming the work you do, showing the deliverable you produce, and using contrast language that separates strategy/planning from channel management. Practical moves you can make now: 1) Short service line — replace any “social content” shorthand with a single sentence that states the outcome and the deliverable, e.g. “I help you pick a clear content direction and deliver a practical posting plan you can run or hand off.” 2) Package language — list what’s included and excluded. Example: Included — strategy session, content pillars, 4-week content calendar, post templates. Excluded — channel posting, community moderation (available as an optional retainer). 3) Visual evidence — show a real sample (screenshot or PDF) of the planning work you hand clients: a one‑page plan or a week-of-posts template. 4) Intake and conversations — add a short line to your enquiry form and email auto-reply that asks whether they want strategy only or also hands-on management, and confirm which they mean before calls. 5) Pricing cues — price the strategy package separately and show a clearly labeled “execution” add-on so buyers see the difference at a glance. 6) Microcopy fixes — use verbs that describe what you do: “clarify, plan, template, schedule” and avoid “manage” or “run” unless it’s an option. Sample microcopy you can paste: • Headline: “Content direction and a plan you can actually use.” • One-line offer: “We clarify your focus, pick three content pillars, and hand you a 4‑week calendar with templates — you post it or we can manage it for you.” • FAQ bullet: “Do you post for me or just make the plan؟” Answer: “I create the strategy and the hands-on plan. Posting and moderation are optional add-ons.” 7) Show process not aspiration — on the services page use a 3-step visual (Discover → Decide → Deliver) with the deliverable named at step 3. 8) Contract clarity — include a simple scope sentence in your meeting confirmation and proposal that restates responsibilities. These changes preserve your existing niche and make everyday enquiries less confusing without inventing a new offer.
